### Added
- `modelManager.networkPolicy.egress` (`fqdns`, `cidrs`, both empty): further destinations of model-manager on 443 whatever the backend — a private identity provider, a model mirror — the same knob `agentManager.networkPolicy.egress` already is. cilium: FQDN selectors next to the Hugging Face names and the Ollama endpoint, blocks as `toCIDR`; kubernetes: the blocks as `ipBlock`s (names are ignored, the flavor has no FQDN selector). `networkPolicy.additionalEgressCIDRs` / `additionalEgressFQDNs` now apply to the model-manager cilium egress for the ollama backend too (they used to render only for the kserve backend; the kubernetes flavor always applied them).
- `agent-platform.idpHosts` helper in the connectivity chart: the hosts a service that validates tokens itself reaches at its identity provider, from the OAuth provider and the issuer URL — the Dex issuer host, or Google's `accounts.google.com`, `www.googleapis.com` and `oauth2.googleapis.com`. `agent-platform.idpEgress.cilium` takes `provider` next to `issuerUrl` and renders one `toFQDNs` rule over those hosts.
### Fixed
- The model-manager and agent-manager cilium network policies open egress to Google when the component validates tokens with `oauth.provider: google`. The IdP egress rule named the issuer host by FQDN and the per-component issuer helpers deliberately return nothing for the google provider, so a Google-backed install rendered no name at all: mcp-oauth's JWKS fetch (`www.googleapis.com/oauth2/v3/certs`), userinfo fallback and discovery (`accounts.google.com`) timed out under `policyEnforcementMode: always`, muster's forwarded-token sessions failed and the operator had to add the three hosts to `agentManager.networkPolicy.egress.fqdns` and open `world:443` for model-manager by hand (agent-platform-standalone#106). The rule now derives the hosts from the provider: `accounts.google.com` (discovery, authorization), `www.googleapis.com` (JWKS, userinfo) and `oauth2.googleapis.com` (token, revocation) — the endpoints mcp-oauth's google provider dials — next to the unchanged cluster entity on 443/10443. The dex render is byte-identical; the kubernetes flavor already opened every public destination on 443 while OAuth is on. `make verify-managers` asserts both providers and the new egress knob.
